changeSet.sql:
INSERT INTO practice_revision ( practice_id, revision_number, criteria, created_at, slug, name, applies_to, trigger_events, precompute_script, why_it_matters, what_good_looks_like, area_slug, area_name, area_description, area_icon, area_color, detection_fingerprint, automated_review_policy ) SELECT practice.id, COALESCE(( SELECT MAX(existing.revision_number) + 1 FROM practice_revision existing WHERE existing.practice_id = practice.id ), 1), practice.criteria, now(), practice.slug, practice.name, practice.applies_to, practice.trigger_events, practice.precompute_script, practice.why_it_matters, practice.what_good_looks_like, area.slug, area.name, area.description, area.icon, area.color, NULL, practice.automated_review_policy FROM practice LEFT JOIN practice_area area ON area.id = practice.practice_area_id;
UPDATE practice SET current_revision_id = revision.id FROM practice_revision revision WHERE revision.practice_id = practice.id AND revision.automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL AND revision.revision_number = ( SELECT MAX(candidate.revision_number) FROM practice_revision candidate WHERE candidate.practice_id = practice.id AND candidate.automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL );

UPDATE practice SET current_revision_id = previous.id, slug = previous.slug, name = previous.name, applies_to = previous.applies_to, trigger_events = previous.trigger_events, criteria = previous.criteria, precompute_script = previous.precompute_script, why_it_matters = previous.why_it_matters, what_good_looks_like = previous.what_good_looks_like, practice_area_id = ( SELECT area.id FROM practice_area area WHERE area.workspace_id = practice.workspace_id AND area.slug = previous.area_slug ) FROM practice_revision boundary JOIN practice_revision previous ON previous.practice_id = boundary.practice_id AND previous.revision_number = boundary.revision_number - 1 WHERE boundary.practice_id = practice.id AND boundary.automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL AND previous.automated_review_policy IS NULL AND boundary.revision_number = ( SELECT MIN(candidate.revision_number) FROM practice_revision candidate JOIN practice_revision before_candidate ON before_candidate.practice_id = candidate.practice_id AND before_candidate.revision_number = candidate.revision_number - 1 WHERE candidate.practice_id = practice.id AND candidate.automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL AND before_candidate.automated_review_policy IS NULL );
-- Only the revisions THIS migration inserted, which is exactly one per practice: the -- lowest-numbered revision that carries a policy. Deleting every policy-carrying revision -- instead would take out every revision authored since the migration ran, and -- observation.practice_revision_id is ON DELETE SET NULL — so a rollback would silently -- unpin the criteria that every observation since was judged against, with no error and -- nothing to reconstruct them from. DELETE FROM practice_revision pr WHERE pr.automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL AND pr.revision_number = ( SELECT MIN(candidate.revision_number) FROM practice_revision candidate WHERE candidate.practice_id = pr.practice_id AND candidate.automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL );

changeSet.comment: Keep the readiness decisions out of the evidence snapshot so they can be read in bulk.
changeSet.sql:
-- A snapshot carries one entry per staged file, so a repository-tree capture makes it -- megabytes. Postgres cannot read one key out of a TOASTed jsonb without detoasting the -- whole value, so reporting on 200 reviews meant decompressing 200 snapshots for a few -- kilobytes of answer. The decisions move to their own column; the snapshot stays put. UPDATE agent_job SET review_readiness = evidence_snapshot -> 'automatedReviewReadiness' WHERE jsonb_typeof(evidence_snapshot) = 'object' AND jsonb_exists(evidence_snapshot, 'automatedReviewReadiness');
-- The snapshot stored the source manifest twice: once as the bytes staged in the sandbox -- and once as the object they were rendered from. Nothing ever read the second copy. UPDATE agent_job SET evidence_snapshot = evidence_snapshot - 'artifactSourceManifest' WHERE jsonb_typeof(evidence_snapshot) = 'object' AND jsonb_exists(evidence_snapshot, 'artifactSourceManifest');

changeSet.comment: One list of needs with a stance, and capture strictness read off the source contract.
changeSet.sql:
-- Two lists that differed only in whether an absent source refused the review, and a -- completeness/content pair restated on every entry that every practice had already spelled -- the same way for a given source. The stance survives as a word; the strictness moves to the -- source contract, so it is dropped here rather than carried. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION migrate_policy_to_needs(policy jsonb) RETURNS jsonb LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $migrate_needs$ SELECT (policy - 'requiredEvidence' - 'optionalContext') || jsonb_build_object('needs', COALESCE(( SELECT jsonb_agg(need ORDER BY need->>'sourceKind') FROM ( SELECT jsonb_build_object('sourceKind', entry->>'sourceKind', 'stance', 'REQUIRED') AS need FROM jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(policy->'requiredEvidence', '[]'::jsonb)) AS entry UNION ALL SELECT jsonb_build_object('sourceKind', entry->>'sourceKind', 'stance', 'CONTEXTUAL') AS need FROM jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(policy->'optionalContext', '[]'::jsonb)) AS entry ) AS needs ), '[]'::jsonb)) $migrate_needs$;
UPDATE practice SET automated_review_policy = migrate_policy_to_needs(automated_review_policy) WHERE jsonb_exists(automated_review_policy, 'requiredEvidence'); UPDATE curated_practice_override SET automated_review_policy = migrate_policy_to_needs(automated_review_policy) WHERE automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_exists(automated_review_policy, 'requiredEvidence'); ALTER TABLE practice_revision DISABLE TRIGGER practice_revision_immutable_update; UPDATE practice_revision SET automated_review_policy = migrate_policy_to_needs(automated_review_policy) WHERE automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_exists(automated_review_policy, 'requiredEvidence'); -- Same reason as -21: the policy digest feeds the review-rule fingerprint, so every stored -- one now describes a policy shape that no longer exists. CatalogProvenanceBackfill -- recomputes them on the next boot. UPDATE practice_revision SET review_rule_fingerprint = NULL WHERE slug IS NOT NULL AND automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE practice_revision ENABLE TRIGGER practice_revision_immutable_update; DROP FUNCTION migrate_policy_to_needs(jsonb);

-- The stance is recoverable; the strictness is not, because it is no longer written per -- practice anywhere. It is restored from the source contract as it stood when this -- changeset ran, which is the same value every practice had stated — that equality is -- what licensed moving it, and is pinned by EvidencePolicyRedundancyTest. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION restore_policy_evidence_lists(policy jsonb) RETURNS jsonb LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $restore_lists$ SELECT (policy - 'needs') || jsonb_build_object('requiredEvidence', COALESCE(( SELECT jsonb_agg( CASE entry->>'sourceKind' WHEN 'scm.pull-request.diff' THEN jsonb_build_object( 'sourceKind', entry->>'sourceKind', 'completeness', 'COMPLETE', 'content', 'NON_EMPTY') WHEN 'scm.pull-request.core' THEN jsonb_build_object( 'sourceKind', entry->>'sourceKind', 'completeness', 'COMPLETE') WHEN 'scm.issue.core' THEN jsonb_build_object( 'sourceKind', entry->>'sourceKind', 'completeness', 'COMPLETE') WHEN 'slack.conversation.thread' THEN jsonb_build_object( 'sourceKind', entry->>'sourceKind', 'completeness', 'COMPLETE') ELSE jsonb_build_object( 'sourceKind', entry->>'sourceKind', 'completeness', 'NO_REQUIREMENT') END ORDER BY entry->>'sourceKind') FROM jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(policy->'needs', '[]'::jsonb)) AS entry WHERE entry->>'stance' = 'REQUIRED' ), '[]'::jsonb)) || jsonb_build_object('optionalContext', COALESCE(( SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('sourceKind', entry->>'sourceKind') ORDER BY entry->>'sourceKind') FROM jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(policy->'needs', '[]'::jsonb)) AS entry WHERE entry->>'stance' = 'CONTEXTUAL' ), '[]'::jsonb)); $restore_lists$;
UPDATE practice SET automated_review_policy = restore_policy_evidence_lists(automated_review_policy) WHERE jsonb_exists(automated_review_policy, 'needs'); UPDATE curated_practice_override SET automated_review_policy = restore_policy_evidence_lists(automated_review_policy) WHERE automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_exists(automated_review_policy, 'needs'); ALTER TABLE practice_revision DISABLE TRIGGER practice_revision_immutable_update; UPDATE practice_revision SET automated_review_policy = restore_policy_evidence_lists(automated_review_policy) WHERE automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_exists(automated_review_policy, 'needs'); UPDATE practice_revision SET review_rule_fingerprint = NULL WHERE slug IS NOT NULL AND automated_review_policy IS NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE practice_revision ENABLE TRIGGER practice_revision_immutable_update; DROP FUNCTION restore_policy_evidence_lists(jsonb);

changeSet.author: hephaestus-readiness
changeSet.comment:
Record that a job's feedback-preparation lanes ran, so work a rejected async submission dropped can be found again.
Both lanes hang off one AFTER_COMMIT @Async event. The event is published once, the executor is bounded, and a rejection lands in a transaction-synchronisation callback where no lane code runs — so a saturated pool silently prepared nothing for whoever happened to finish during it. Absence of feedback rows cannot stand in for these columns: both lanes legitimately prepare nothing very often, so "no rows" does not distinguish a lane that decided from a lane that never ran, and a sweep built on it would re-route every recent job on every pass forever.
Deliberately NOT backfilled. Every row is left null, and the recovery sweep only looks back a bounded window, so exactly one thing happens on the first pass after this migration: jobs that finished inside that window are re-offered to both lanes once. That is the desired outcome, not a cost — the preparers are idempotent on (agent_job_id, position), so a job whose lanes did run writes nothing, and one whose lanes were dropped by the deploy itself is recovered. Everything older is outside the window and never selected.

changeSet.author: hephaestus-readiness
changeSet.comment: The recovery sweep's index. Partial on purpose: the predicate it serves is "finished and at least one lane unmarked", which is the empty set on a healthy instance and a handful of rows after an incident. A row leaves the index the moment its lanes are marked, so this stays kilobytes on an agent_job table of any size — where a plain index on completed_at would grow with the whole job history to answer a question about a few rows, and no index at all would put a sequential scan of that history on an hourly schedule.

changeSet.author: hephaestus-readiness
changeSet.comment:
Say which of the two spend records a ledger row's token counts came from.
An attempt is billed the per-bucket maximum of the runner's own report and the proxy's per-call accumulation, because neither is complete: compaction deletes calls from the runner's report, and the proxy sees no streamed call and no cache write. That maximum is the right amount, but it means a MERGED row matches neither source's own number, so without this column an amount cannot be reconciled against anything. It is equally the signal for the defect that forced the change — a run of PROXY rows where RUNNER is expected is compaction eating calls, which had the ledger booking a quarter of real spend while the budget cap read it.
Nullable, and rows written before it are left null rather than guessed at: the old code preferred the runner's report whenever it was non-zero, so an existing row is 'whatever that rule produced', which is not one of these values.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE llm_usage_event ADD CONSTRAINT ck_llm_usage_event_usage_provenance CHECK (usage_provenance IS NULL OR usage_provenance IN ('RUNNER', 'PROXY', 'MERGED', 'NONE'));

changeSet.author: hephaestus-readiness
changeSet.comment:
Make "unpriced" mean one thing.
Two live queries asked whether a month had unresolvable spend and disagreed: existsUnpricedInstanceFunded — the one that blocks every job in the workspace — reads pricing_state, while countUncosted — the number the operator sees — read cost_usd IS NULL. Every path in the application writes rows where those agree. The 1785015307013 ledger backfill did not: it classified a zero-cost row that had burned real tokens as UNPRICED and stored the zero. Such a row blocks the cap and is invisible to the count, which is how an operator came to read "1 unpriced event" off a month with nineteen holding the cap shut.
The repair sets cost_usd back to NULL on exactly those rows, which is what an unresolvable price has always meant. It moves no total: every sum filters on pricing_state = 'PRICED', so these rows contributed nothing before and contribute nothing now. It is deliberately narrow — only rows that are UNPRICED with a cost — so a PRICED or NO_CHARGE amount is never touched.
The constraint is the part that lasts. With it the two columns cannot part again, and the reprice path (which is the only UPDATE the ledger permits) cannot leave a row half-moved: setting pricing_state without a cost, or a cost without the state, now fails loudly instead of producing another invisible blocker.

rollback.sql: ALTER TABLE llm_usage_event DROP CONSTRAINT ck_llm_usage_event_unpriced_has_no_cost;
